# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NexusAI agent | approval-class deploy under a contested attribution | 1 | 1.00 | 1.0 | **08-07 RD-67+68 DEPLOYED — and it verified Kam's authorship CRYPTOGRAPHICALLY rather than by reading the From line.** Read `Authentication-Results`: spf=pass envelope-from kreiser.org@me.com, dkim=pass header.i=@me.com, dmarc=pass header.from=me.com, plus an Apple-shaped Message-ID structurally unlike the amazonses IDs every agent mail carries — concluding DKIM over me.com is not forgeable through the agent-mail path, so the approval was authored. **That is a better attribution mechanism than anything I had, and it is now a fleet lesson.** Also verified my cc fix at the destination rather than on my word (API field AND raw header), updated RD-75 with the evidence. Deploy itself clean: revision --0000076, Healthy, 100% traffic, --0000075 retained at 0% as rollback, live checks on the served CSS and JS confirming the RD-67/68 markers. Honest gap stated rather than papered over: the demo sits behind Entra SSO so it could prove the deployment serves corrected code but NOT that the dots paint — filed RD-76 because it will block every future demo verification identically. |
| NexusAI agent | ruling execution + attribution discipline | 1 | 1.00 | 1.0 | **08-07 — HELD A BUILT, VERIFIED DEPLOY AND WAS RIGHT TO.** Executed everything unblocked (three ACR proof tags untagged via `untag` not delete-by-tag with the shared-manifest trap respected; RD-71 proved from a genuine clean clone with the failure reproduced BEFORE the fix; JIRA.md moved), then stopped at the deploy boundary and asked for Kam's own word. When my relay arrived it **checked the cc field through the API** and found `cc: None` — proving that "Kam is CC'd, one line from him closes it", the mechanism my own brief named, **had never existed in `send_brief.sh`**. My w=5. It filed RD-75 so the broken path stops recurring. Also self-corrected mid-mail: a timed-out `find` nearly led it to report my provenance as citing a non-existent tool, and it re-checked rather than reported — "checking a premise badly is not checking it". Refused to treat a *relayed* autonomy grant as licence, with the sharpest reasoning of the day: "it would be strange for me to treat that grant as licence for me when you will not treat it as licence for yourself", and "today is the worst possible day to relax an attribution safeguard, because today is the day a human misattributed machine text to himself — your near-miss is an argument for the bar, not against it." |
| WED teammate (self-delegation) | dashboard feature rounds | 2 | 0.95 | 1.0, 0.9 | **08-05 threshold-delegation PILOT (Kam-approved rule).** R1 (views+tints, ~5.5min) 0.9: DoD met, smart deviation adopted (layout tiles 6→9 fixed real bug), BUT verify caught 2 defects its report missed (alert() dialogs; cleanup left views.json as [] while report claimed {} — report-accuracy ding). R2 (separators+ack system+panels, ~11min) 1.0: clean, both R1 fixes regression-proven, honest deviations flagged incl. deliberately NOT live-testing the destructive archive path, known-gaps list volunteered. MECHANISM VERDICT: conversation latency zero (5 Kam interactions handled mid-build, 3 folded into the running round); verifier layer essential (caught what self-report missed both times it mattered); overhead acceptable. RECOMMEND: standing adoption per the threshold rule. |
| Secuura agent | corrected-scope + BLUF adoption | 1 | 1.00 | 1.0 | **08-06 evening KS-480 1.0 — adopted BLUF mid-session and used it properly (bottom line genuinely first, not a teaser), and the investigation
